newsitem.title: USA: NYS Speaker to back partial LILCO takeover - paper.
newsitem.headline: NYS Speaker to back partial LILCO takeover - paper.

text.p: The New York State Assembly Speaker, who could veto Governor George Pataki's proposal for a partial state takeover of Long Island Lighting Co, will back it if he gets assurances, Newsday said on Tuesday.

The paper said that while Sheldon Silver, D-Manhattan, was uncomfortable with aspects of Pataki's, which include selling $7.3 billion of tax-exempt debt, he will support it because coming changes in federal tax rules will make it impossible to substantially cut electricity rates in the future.

In an interview with Silver, Newsday quoted him as saying: "Unfortunately, the plan has been negotiated already and in order to be realistic...I will vote for the plan on Wednesday, provided that certain assurances are met."

The assurances Silver seeks include getting the parties to guarantee, in writing, how much rates will drop over the next 10 years. And Silver told Newsday he wants LILCO, which plans to merge with Brooklyn Union Gas, to assure the state it will spend at least half the money it is paid for its assets on developing Long Island's energy infrastructure.

Silver, Pataki and the Senate Majority Leader, Joseph Bruno, R-Troy, each hold one of three seats on the state Public Authorities Control Board, which must approve tax-exempt bond sales. The board next is scheduled to meet on Wednesday, and the plan for the Long Island Power Authority to buy assets from LILCO and Brooklyn Union Gas is on the agenda.

Much of the savings produced under the governor's plan rely on the tax-exempt bond sale--the nation's largest--and the Internal Revenue Service would have to hold that LILCO shareholders were not subject to a $2 billion capital gains tax for the deal to go forward. The federal tax agency was expected to soon publish new rules governing how such transactions treated.

Silver, who spoke to Newsday with the understanding that his comments would remain confidential until they were published, told the paper he planned on Tuesday to give the governor his conditions in writing.

A spokesman for LILCO, who was not specifically commenting on Silver's remarks, told the paper that the utility has to reinvest the money from the sale or pay tax on it, adding it expects to invest in Long Island.
He added LILCO already had guaranteed some savings from its proposed merger with Brooklyn Union Gas, adding the remaining savings would be produced by the tax-exempt financing plan.

Silver's remarks to Newsday go further than other published reports. For example, the New York Post, in its Tuesday edition, quoted Silver as saying "There are a lot of alternatives to (Pataki plan)."
